subject: Issue with Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test in lavaan when Using Clusters

messages.author: 1933d661a0a10f37
messages.subject: Issue with Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test in lavaan when Using Clusters
parts:
Hi everyone,

I’m trying to compare two CFA models using a chi-squared difference test with anova() in lavaan. 

# One-Factor-Model
model1 <- '
            LatentFactor1 =~ Var1 + Var2 + Var3 + Var4 + Var5 + Var6 + Var7
'

fit1 <- cfa(model1, data = data, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml", cluster = "GroupID", std.lv = TRUE)
summary(fit1, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

# Two-Factor Model
model2 <- '
            LatentFactor1 =~ Var1 + Var3 + Var4
            LatentFactor2 =~ Var2 + Var5 + Var6 + Var7
'

fit2 <- cfa(model2, data = data, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml", orthogonal = FALSE, cluster = "GroupID", std.lv = TRUE)
summary(fit2, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

# model comparison
anova(fit1, fit2)

When I include the cluster argument (cluster = "GroupID"), I encounter the following output and warnings:

Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test (method = "satorra.bentler.2001")  

lavaan->lavTestLRT():  
   lavaan NOTE: The "Chisq" column contains standard test statistics, not the robust test that should be reported per model. A robust difference test  
   is a function of two standard (not robust) statistics.  
        Df   AIC   BIC   Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)  
fit_ca2 13 19913 20022  58.542                                
fit_ca1 14 20040 20144 187.508                  1            
Warning message:  
lavaan->lav_test_diff_SatorraBentler2001():  
   scaling factor is negative  

When I remove the cluster argument, the output is as expected:

Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test (method = "satorra.bentler.2001")  

lavaan->lavTestLRT():  
   lavaan NOTE: The "Chisq" column contains standard test statistics, not the robust test that should be reported per model. A robust difference test  
   is a function of two standard (not robust) statistics.  
        Df   AIC   BIC   Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)  
fit_ca2 13 19913 20022  58.542                                
fit_ca1 14 20040 20144 187.508     184.59       1  < 2.2e-16 ***  
---  
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1  

I’ve also tried using lavTestLRT(fit_ca1, fit_ca2, method = "satorra.bentler.2010"), but it doesn’t work either.

My Questions:
  1. What does the warning about the negative scaling factor mean?
  2. Why does the test fail when clustering is included, and how could this be resolved?

From my understanding, the scaling factor being negative might suggest issues with model fit or convergence, but I’m unsure why it occurs specifically when using clustering.
